acceptance: `evolve salvage list --json` on a fixture salvage directory prints each leaf's cycle, HEAD, patch stats and landed flag (red: unknown subcommand "list")
An unreadable leaf exits 2 naming it; an empty or missing directory prints nothing and exits 0
gc and the list read one exported salvage-path helper
fix: Add `evolve salvage list [--json]`. It prints one row per salvage leaf: cycle, branch, HEAD, changed-file count and patch size, untracked-file count, age, and whether the HEAD is already in origin/main (landed). It reads the layout through one path helper exported from internal/gc, so gc and the list agree. It is read-only: exit 0, or exit 2 naming a leaf it cannot read. Document it in runtime-reference.md next to `evolve gc`.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: `evolve gc` salvages a dirty or unmerged cycle worktree before removing it, writing .evolve/operator-salvage/<leaf>/{HEAD,uncommitted.patch,untracked.tgz} (internal/gc/salvage.go:118; runtime-reference.md:205). operating-policy.md:85 says to inventory a failed cycle's work before re-queueing it. `evolve salvage` has one subcommand, `report`, which gives the bad_verdict rate (cmd_salvage.go:21). The operator lists the directory, reads each HEAD and sizes each patch by hand.
title: `evolve salvage` reports only the bad-verdict rate; add `salvage list` to inventory what gc salvaged
